messages.subject: [R-sig-Debian] APT key for cloud.r-project.org expired
messages.body_plain:
Dear CRAN Debian backport users,

yes, this is an issue for Debian bookworm. One way to solve it right away is 
to use/upgrade to trixie, which considers the signatures still valid, as the 
key was not expired when the repositories were signed.

I am currently travelling, but plan to generate a new key on Thursday morning 
(not sure how much time it will take, the last time I did was five years 
ago...) and sign the repos with the updated key in order to satisfy apt from 
bookworm.

Another way would be add trusted = yes to the corresponding entry in your apt 
source.list, but I think this completely skips signature verification so in 
case one of my systems gets compromised, you may get malware. In case you 
decide to do this anyways, make sure to revert it after I have published the 
new key.

Cheers,

Johannes

On Dienstag, 17. November 2026 17:02:55 Mitteleuropäische Normalzeit Niels 
Hendriks wrote:
> Hello,
> 
> 
> I initially posted to r-help at R-project.org and was redirected here, so
> hopefully this is the right place:
> 
> 
> 
> 
> The APT key for the repository at cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/debian has
> expired.  The key is documented at
> https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/debian/#secure-apt and it expired a
> few days ago:
> https://keyserver.ubuntu.com/pks/lookup?search=0x95C0FAF38DB3CCAD0C080A7BDC
> 78B2DDEABC47B7&fingerprint=on&op=vindex
> 
> 
> Because of this, the packages can no longer be installed:
> 
> W: An error occurred during the signature verification. The repository is
> not updated and the previous index files will be used. GPG error:
> http://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/debian bookworm-cran40/ InRelease: The
> following signatures were invalid: EXPKEYSIG B8F25A8A73EACF41 Johannes
> Ranke <johannes.ranke at jrwb.de> W: Failed to fetch
> http://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/debian/bookworm-cran40/InRelease  The
> following signatures were invalid: EXPKEYSIG B8F25A8A73EACF41 Johannes
> Ranke <johannes.ranke at jrwb.de>
> 
> 
> I also tested bookworm-cran46 instead of bookworm-cran40, but this uses the
> same key signature, so it gives the same error.
> 
> 
> Could the packages be updated with a new key?
> 
> 
> Thank you!
> Niels Hendriks
